title: No registration path for third-party attestors; availability probe is not part of the Attestor trait
description:
hire-attestors/src/registry.rs:19-93 — `probe_sources()` returns `Vec<Arc<dyn Attestor>>` built from a hardcoded list of the eight in-tree attestors. There is no `register()`, no builder, no `Registry` type, and the returned Vec is the only public entry point. A downstream crate that implements `Attestor` has no supported way to get it into the set the daemon uses; it must reimplement probe_sources and every consumer of it.

Second half of the same problem: the availability check `is_available()` is not a method on the `Attestor` trait (hire-attestors/src/lib.rs:108-136). It exists only as an inherent function on each concrete type, and its signature is not even consistent between them: `TailscaleAttestor::is_available(&self)` (tailscale.rs:28) takes self, while ssh.rs:32, did_key.rs:23, fido2.rs:32, goa.rs:27, gpg.rs:22, piv.rs:25 are all associated functions with no receiver. Because the check lives outside the trait, `Arc<dyn Attestor>` cannot be probed at all, which is why registry.rs must know each concrete type.

Concretely for a caller: you cannot write `fn add_attestor(a: Arc<dyn Attestor>)` against this crate and have it participate in startup probing or in the "skip unavailable sources, never fatal" behaviour the README promises.

Fix before 1.0: put `async fn is_available(&self) -> bool` (or fold it into `enumerate()` returning empty) on the trait, and make probe_sources take/return a registry that accepts externally supplied `Arc<dyn Attestor>`.
